episodes.212002: During the afternoon, evening, and late evening hours of May 18th, supercells brought severe weather to far NW Missouri. Storms eventually congealed into a large line of thunderstorms, which brought widespread damaging wind gusts to the region as well as a couple tornadoes.
episodes.212013: During the 19th afternoon, an unstable airmass ahead of an approaching surface trough triggered a cluster of severe thunderstorms across central Indiana.  Convection initially intensified over the western and northern portions of the Indianapolis metropolitan area shortly after 1500 EST, capitalizing on strong low-to-mid level wind shear. These storms quickly organized into severe segments that tracked eastward and southward, producing a concentrated swath of damaging straight-line winds across Hendricks, Hamilton, Delaware, and Bartholomew counties before exiting the IND CWA by 1700 EST.||Damaging winds were the primary hazard with this event, resulting in structural damage, power outages, and travel disruptions. Hamilton County was particularly hard hit, where estimated wind gusts up to 55 knots (63 mph) downed multiple utility lines, left a power pole leaning in Noblesville, and knocked a large tree through the roof of a residence.  Transportation infrastructure was also impacted:  in Delaware County, estimated gusts of 55 knots blew over a semi truck on Interstate 69 near mile marker 249.  Earlier in the afternoon, severe gusts in Hendricks County downed several trees, including one that blocked a roadway southwest of Danville.  As the severe weather pushed into south-central Indiana, the KBAK AWOS at Columbus Municipal Airport in Bartholomew County recorded a peak measured wind gust of 52 knots (60 mph).
episodes.212058: Supercell thunderstorms developed ahead of a dryline and near a warm front during the afternoon and evening hours of May 18.  The storms produced 7 documented tornadoes and eventually evolved into a line of storms that produced damaging winds of 60-80 mph across northeast and east central Kansas.  Some areas also received 2-5 inches of rain just two to three hours causing flash flooding in several areas including the city of Manhattan.
episodes.212088: An isolated thunderstorm produced very localized, marginal wind damage just east of Mount Jackson.
episodes.212089: An isolated thunderstorm produced localized gale-force wind gusts over the upper tidal Potomac River.
episodes.212248: A cold front pushed south into west Texas and southeast New Mexico on the 19th. This front stalled in the Trans-Pecos area. A few thunderstorms developed south of this front and east of a dryline in the eastern Permian Basin and Lower Trans-Pecos. One thunderstorm produced large hail in Big Lake while another produced flash flooding in Terrell County.
episodes.212297: A squall line moved through the Great Lakes region, sparking showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.212500: A cold front moved through the Ohio Valley during the afternoon and evening hours. Strong storms developed and produced damaging wind gusts and localized flooding.
episodes.212550: Thunderstorms produced strong winds across the waters and bays.
episodes.212746: A cluster of severe storms which began east of the Sierra Madre Oriental maintained intensity as it propagated eastward across the CWA, eventually making it to the coast and over area waters. This organized segment produced damaging winds across the Brush Country and elevated gusts over the Middle Texas Coastal Waters.
episodes.212870: A two day period of active weather prevailed over West Virginia from May 19th to the 20th amid an advancing cold front. Beginning on the 19th, one sub-severe thunderstorm spilled into Wood County from activity that progressed through southeast Ohio, which resulted in some downed tree limbs. The more impressive round of storms took shape on the 20th as the front encroached on the Central Appalachians. Storms initially tracked into  the southwest portions of West Virginia around peak heating and remained active throughout the course of the evening. Damaging wind gusts associated with storms resulted in a slew of downed trees and power lines across the state. A 60 mile per hour gust was recorded outside of Elkins by a trained spotter as a strong storm swept through. Additionally, storms crossing through the Kanawha Valley grew tall enough to produce large hail for a brief period of time. A swath of 1 to 1.75 inch hailstones were observed from Putnam and Logan Counties over to Kanawha and Clay Counties. The severe risk subsided as the sun began to set for the evening and the cold front began its passage through the forecast area.
episodes.212881: An active weather day transpired on May 19th in southeast Ohio as a quick succession of storms passed through the area. The first round was observed during the late afternoon, when scattered thunderstorm development that moved in a southwest to northeast fashion. This clipped portions of Jackson County and resulted in several downed trees and power lines around the area. A few hours later, a line of thunderstorms slowly progressing through the Ohio Valley arrived into Perry and Morgan Counties around sunset. Decaying storms due to the loss of daytime heating caused downburst winds that promoted hundreds of homes to be without power due to downed trees and power lines. The weakening trend prospered into the late evening hours, bringing the severe threat over southeast Ohio to an end.
episodes.212904: A cluster of severe storms which began east of the Sierra Madre Oriental maintained intensity as it propagated eastward across the CWA, eventually making it to the coast and over area waters. This organized segment produced damaging winds across the Brush Country and elevated gusts over the Middle Texas Coastal Waters.
episodes.212911: Amid unseasonably hot temperatures for the middle of May, isolated thunderstorms formed around southwest Virginia on the afternoon of the 18th. These storms produced damaging wind gusts as they quickly collapsed after their initiation, which resulted in a tree to knock down onto a trailer in the town of Vansant. The loss of daytime heating at sunset brought the threat for additional thunderstorm damage to an end on this particular day.
episodes.212987: An environment ripe with instability and moisture coincided with the eastern edge of an elevated mixed layer (EML) allowed for scattered thunderstorm development during the afternoon and evening hours of May 18, 2026. Due to the lack of extremely favorable shear and lift, these thunderstorms struggled to develop further; however, inverted V soundings did allow for some damaging winds to mix down to the surface across Centre County and Clinton County causing isolated wind damage.
episodes.213122: A thunderstorm complex moved south into eastern Missouri during the early morning of May 18th. Isolated wind damage occurred as wind gusts up to 71 kts blew through the area. Rain lasted the rest of the day, resulting in minor flooding in Warren county.
episodes.213189: Multicell thunderstorms over eastern Indiana moved into northwest Ohio resulting in sporadic reports of damaging wind gusts and sub-severe hail.
episodes.213190: Multicell thunderstorms over eastern Indiana moved into northwest Ohio resulting in sporadic reports of damaging wind gusts and sub-severe hail.
episodes.213211: A cold front brought several days of showers and thunderstorms to the region as it moved through the area, stalled, and then retreated back to the north. Isolated instances of hail, severe winds, and flooding occurred with this activity.
episodes.213224: A slow southward-moving cold front tracked into South-Central Texas, producing a line of strong to severe thunderstorms which advanced ahead of the front as it encountered a moist and unstable airmass on the evening of May 19 into the early hours of May 20. The storms produced swaths of severe winds and some large hail. Locally heavy rain that led to some flash flooding mainly north of the Austin area and in the Hill Country.
episodes.213370: A few (brief) thunderstorms formed off of a dryline across portions of western Oklahoma during the evening of the 18th, producing intermittent reports of large hail and severe thunderstorm winds. Towards the initial hours of the 19th, an organized convective line moved into portions of far northern Oklahoma, producing wind damage across portions of Kay County, near Newkirk.
episodes.213379: A strong upper level trough moved into the Rockies on May 18, with southwest flow aloft over the Missouri Ozarks. A cluster of thunderstorms pushed southeast into portions of central Missouri, bringing heavy rainfall and flash flooding to St. Clair, Benton, and Camden counties. Additionally, a low level jet axis extending from the Gulf through eastern Kansas strengthened overnight into May 19 while interacting with the upper level trough and a surface front. As a result, a second line of thunderstorms formed across northern Kansas, moving into Missouri overnight before exiting the state in the late afternoon hours. With the multiple rounds of heavy rainfall, storm total rainfall observations ranged between 3-7 inches across portions of southeast Kansas and the Missouri Ozarks, with 8.20 inches of rainfall measured in Hickory County. This led to multiple road closures reported from the flooding.
episodes.213426: Several clusters of severe storms developed along a slow moving cold front as it creeped across the area through the afternoon and into the nighttime hours. These storms produced up to 2-inch hail along with estimated winds up to 90 mph. Multiple structures were damaged across south-central Kansas due to these storms.
episodes.213563: A squall line moved through eastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 19th, exiting the area by early afternoon. Pockets of heavy rainfall occurred due to the slow movement of the storms. Some of the storms moved repeatedly over the same areas, which also resulted in locally heavy rainfall. Flash flooding resulted from this rainfall in Miami.
episodes.213564: A squall line moved through eastern Oklahoma and into northwestern Arkansas during the morning of the 19th. The strongest thunderstorms within the line produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.213591: Easterly sea breeze convection produces a strong marine gust over Tampa Bay.
episodes.213628: One late-evening severe thunderstorm tracked northeast across Tucker County, West Virginia and produced wind damage knocking down a large tree across a highway. Despite some MLCIN in place, MUCAPE values still reached up to 1000 J/kg and very high DCAPE values up to 1300 J/kg supported sufficient downdraft acceleration to result in tree damage.
episodes.213740: Several cooridors of strong to severe thunderstorms developed along a pre-frontal trough, and migrated across portions of southeast Michigan during the afternoon and early evening hours on Tuesday, May 19th.  These storms brought strong and damaging winds, which resulted in numerous areas sustaining microburst and straight-line wind damage.  Several gusts in excess of 55 mph were recorded along with wind damage leading to numerous downed trees and large limbs, in addition to powerlines.
episodes.213741: Thunderstorms tracking through Lake St. Clair produced wind gusts in excess of 60 knots.
episodes.213742: A thunderstorm moving into western Lake Erie produced a wind gust to 35 knots.
episodes.213746: On the afternoon of May 18, severe thunderstorms produced tornadoes, damaging winds gusts, hail and flash flooding across southeast Nebraska. a strong shortwave trough ejected eastward across the region, providing robust forcing for large-scale ascent. Despite lingering morning cloud cover, very steep mid-level lapse rates combined with the daytime heating of a moist low-level airmass to generate strong instability south of an advancing cold front. Mesoanalysis revealed strong theta-e advection extending from central Kansas through southeast Nebraska and southwest Iowa, highlighting the rapid return of a highly volatile environment. Thunderstorms initially initiated on the warm side of the boundary over northwest Kansas before additional development began over far southeast Nebraska by 2:00 PM CST. This convection initially exhibited discrete supercell characteristics before eventually transitioning into a broader multicell cluster. Additional cells developed north of the cold front across eastern Nebraska, bringing primarily an isolated hail threat. ||The system dropped large hail up to golf ball size (1.75 inches) and generated destructive straight-line winds, including a measured peak gust of 90 mph. The initial supercell storm mode was particularly prolific for tornadogenesis, resulting in 8 tornado across southeast Nebraska. While several of these tornadoes were brief, others caused concentrated damage to trees, farm outbuildings, and irrigation pivots���most notably in Johnson, Nemaha, and Richardson counties. In several instances, these tornadoes were embedded within even broader swaths of intense 80 to 95 mph downburst winds. As the storms transitioned into a messy multicell cluster, torrential downpours also triggered isolated reports of flash flooding.
episodes.213912: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms progressed southeast into portions of extreme Northeast Texas and Southwest Arkansas during the afternoon hours of May 19th, ahead of a weak cold front that became stationary over Southern Oklahoma and portions of North Texas. Storm organization persisted southeast of the front across portions of Northeast Texas and Southwest Arkansas, where modest instability and an attendant gust front ahead of the storms focused renewed development within a moist and unstable air mass. As a result, a few of these storms became strong/severe, which downed a couple of trees near Hope and Lewisville in Hempstead/Lafayette Counties. These storms weakened further later in the afternoon/evening as they exited the area.
episodes.213913: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms progressed southeast into portions of extreme Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana during the afternoon hours of May 19th, ahead of a weak cold front that became stationary over Southern Oklahoma and portions of North Texas. Storm organization persisted southeast of the front across portions of Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and into portions of Northwest Louisiana, where modest instability and an attendant gust front ahead of the storms focused renewed development within a moist and unstable air mass. As a result, a few of these storms became strong/severe across portions of Southwest Arkansas, and again in Bienville Parish in Northwest Louisiana, where several trees were downed southwest of the Mount Lebanon community. These storms weakened further by late afternoon/early evening as they exited the area.
episodes.214064: A few severe thunderstorms produced large hail across the Concho Valley and Northern Edwards Plateau. Also, a lightning strike destroyed a hotel in Brady.
episodes.214094: A line of thunderstorms swept across Lake Erie during the afternoon and evening of Tuesday, May 19, 2026. Several severe thunderstorms within this line generated marine wind gusts over Lake Erie.
episodes.214103: A line of thunderstorms swept across Lake Erie during the afternoon and evening of Monday, May 19, 2026. Several severe thunderstorms within this line generated thunderstorm wind damage and wind gusts across Northern Ohio.
episodes.214126: A series of short waves traversed the region during late May. This provided multiple rounds of storms along the gulf coast.
episodes.214137: On May 18th into May 19th, the Ohio Valley was in the middle of a southwest mid- and upper-level flow regime between troughing over the central CONUS and southeast US ridging. Smaller scale perturbations within the broader flow pattern would support a couple waves of showers and thunderstorms, with isolated strong to severe storms occurring across north central Kentucky and southern Indiana during the afternoon and evening hours both days. On May 18th, storms which initially developed as scattered cells over southern Illinois merged into a line across southern Indiana. This line of storms had a modest amount of instability and vertical wind shear to support it, with temperatures in the upper 80s and dewpoint temperatures in the upper 60s supporting 1500-2000 J/kg of mixed-layer CAPE. Scattered wind damage was observed across southern Indiana, with the greatest concentration of damage occurring in Dubois and Washington County, where several trees were blown down. Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms later in the evening would also lead to a few occurrences of flash flooding, especially along tributaries of the Blue River in Washington County.
episodes.214139: On May 18th into May 19th, the Ohio Valley was in the middle of a southwest mid- and upper-level flow regime between troughing over the central CONUS and southeast US ridging. Smaller scale perturbations within the broader flow pattern would support a couple waves of showers and thunderstorms, with isolated strong to severe storms occurring across north central Kentucky and southern Indiana during the afternoon and evening hours both days. During the afternoon and early evening hours on May 19th, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along the Ohio River, with storms moving from southwest to northeast across northern Kentucky and southern Indiana. While effective bulk shear was relatively unsupportive of organized convection around 20 knots, a few stronger cores were able to develop thanks to 2000-2500 J/kg of mixed-layer CAPE. These stronger cells were able to produce a few instances of wind damage vai downed trees as well as near-severe level hail.

NWS Damage Survey team confirmed a tornado occurred Monday evening, 5/18/2026, beginning at 9:47 PM CDT in southwestern Ray County Missouri. This tornado caused primarily tree damage along its path, but did impact two properties, one north of Fishing River, shortly after the tornado developed. EF1 Damage to two power poles, one out building was noted, along with the roll over of an empty livestock trailer. The tornado resulted in widespread EF1 tree damage near Reynolds Road and W 108th Street. The tornado continued east-northeast, crossing highway 10 south of Elkhorn before causing tree damage north of Swanwick before crossing highway 13. The tornado ended near the intersection of Frazier Road and Millville Road at 10:06 PM CDT.
